tweets.text: Already own an Apple Watch and wondering if an Oura Ring is worth adding just for sleep tracking? Same general idea, very different results. Here's what actually changes 🧵

Quick breakdown before you spend more money:
・Sensor location: wrist vs finger → different accuracy for deep sleep/REM
・Comfort: Oura's low profile beats a watch case for side sleepers
・Neither device is a medical-grade sleep monitor
・Oura adds a monthly membership fee on top of the ring price
・Apple Watch already covers "good enough" tracking for casual users

Before: relying only on Apple Watch, guessing why "sleep score" never lines up with how rested you actually feel.
After: adding a finger-based tracker fills in the blind spots on deep sleep and REM — but only if you're someone who actually acts on the data, not just checks it once.

Full comparison table, who should add Oura Ring 4 vs who should stick with Apple Watch alone, and whether the membership fee is worth it: https://lionlion0201-jpg.github.io/home-recovery-blog/posts/apple-watch-vs-oura-ring-sleep-tracking/
